html:
Kakheti-Hereti was a Georgian kingdom in the east of today's Georgia, centred on the Kakheti valley, with its capital at Telavi. It existed from about 1014 to 1104 and is shown here in 1100.

Kakheti and its neighbour Hereti had been separate principalities. Kvirike III the Great of Kakheti beat the ruler of Hereti and crowned himself king of both, at a time when Bagrat III was uniting the rest of Georgia into the Kingdom of Georgia. Kakheti-Hereti stayed outside.

In the 1060s the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan invaded, and its king Aghsartan I submitted and converted to Islam for a time. In 1104 David IV annexed it, completing the union of the Georgian lands.
